title: The self-improving domain agent
subtitle: The loop that raises the score

slides.heading: The loop
slides.narration: The desk agent improves itself under supervision. One minute shows the loop: the held-out set, the judge, the improver, and the lead who decides what ships.

slides.heading: The held-out set
slides.narration: The loop starts with a held-out set: loan requests the agent never saw, with the librarians' own decisions pinned beside them. The set never enters the queue.

slides.heading: The evaluation run
slides.narration: An evaluation run sets the agent on the held-out set. A judge grades every answer against the pinned decisions, and the scoreboard keeps the score of every version.

slides.heading: The improver reads its mistakes
bullets: It reads what the agent got wrong
It adds one rule per mistake
slides.narration: The improver reads the mistakes, adds one rule to the instructions for each kind, and proposes a new version with its reason. It follows the round's recipe exactly.

slides.heading: The lead decides
bullets: A new version needs the objectives
The rules and limits never change
slides.narration: Nothing ships by itself. A version keeps only when it beats the objectives on the held-out set, the lead approves it, and the loan rules and the approval limit never move.

slides.heading: Why the loop is safe
bullets: The eval set is the contract
The score only tells the truth
slides.narration: The loop stays safe because the eval set is the contract, every round leaves its record, and the scoreboard tells the truth about whether the desk got better.
